population_or_model: Adults (>=18 years) with advanced adrenocortical carcinoma, not candidates for curative surgery, measurable disease, ECOG 0-2, adequate organ function, single centre (MD Anderson); patients exposed to mitotane within 6 months required serum mitotane <2 mg/L
treatment_and_comparator: Oral cabozantinib 60 mg daily as monotherapy, dose reduction permitted; single-arm, no comparator; registered NCT03370718
outcome_numbers: Primary endpoint progression-free survival at 4 months met in 13/18 = 72.2% (95% CI 46.5-90.3); median PFS 6 months (95% CI 4.3-not reached); median follow-up 36.8 months (IQR 30.2-50.3); treatment-related grade >=3 adverse events in 11/18 (61%), one grade 4 hypertension; no treatment-related deaths
source_locator: PubMed record PMID 38608694 (Lancet Oncol 2024), structured abstract Methods, Findings and Interpretation; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03370718
reviewer_notes: Access-completion rerating: at the first pass the source was unavailable and the record was necessarily left uncertain/NA; the official abstract record now supplies design, exposure, primary endpoint and effect estimates. All five strict conditions are met: human ACC population, the named drug is the sole prospectively evaluated intervention, exposure is attributable (true monotherapy, and the mitotane <2 mg/L entry rule removes the CYP3A4 pharmacokinetic confounder that affects other multikinase-inhibitor studies in ACC), the prespecified primary endpoint was met with the authors interpreting the result as promising efficacy, and the design is a registered prospective phase 2 trial well above case-report strength. Transparency caveats that do not change the label under the protocol: the trial is single-arm with no comparator (a design explicitly permitted by the protocol's controlled vocabulary), n=18, industry funding (Exelixis), and access is abstract-only. If the project were to additionally require a randomised comparator for a positive label, this row would become NA; that rule is not in the current protocol.
